(2 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Looks good - the entry accounting, the head/middle/tail split and the copy loop all hold up, and the pool order used is bounded by CDP_EXT_MAX_PAGES so the transient cl_page cp_npgs/cp_len fields still fit. Only optional comments inline, no need to re-spin for them. One thing worth considering for a later patch: the buffer size is now capped and the caller loops instead of failing, which is a user-visible change in how a large unaligned DIO is split, and nothing in sanity.sh appears to exercise it - a case that drives an unaligned DIO past obd_pool_max_objects(0)/2 (a small-memory client, or a fault injection on the cap) would lock that behavior down.

Uploaded patch set 3.

Patch Set 4:

Responses to the AI review; both points are in the new patchset.

COMMIT_MSG (the m4 hunk): the message now describes it and says why it
is an independent build fix -- copy_folio_to_iter() arrived in v5.19
and __filemap_get_folio() in v5.16, so kernels in between did not
build.  Added

    Fixes: 59d84ec3ffb8 ("LU-19249 build: Compatibility updates for kernel v6.16")

Keeping it in this patch rather than splitting it out: the same probe
is what gates LL_DIO_POOL_MAX_ORDER here, so a separate change would
have to land first for this one to be correct.

cl_io.c:1938 (read clamp): right, it is dead, and for exactly the
reason given.  Removed it and LL_DIO_READ_COPY_SPANS with it.

Taking that rather than the other option -- dropping the
HAVE_COPY_FOLIO_TO_ITER term from LL_DIO_POOL_MAX_ORDER -- because
that term is deliberate.  Without copy_folio_to_iter(), a multi-page
entry has to be read back a page at a time, and each pass flushes the
whole folio, so the flushing cost grows with the square of the entry
size.  Order 0 on 5.16-5.18 is the cheaper of the two.  The comment on
LL_DIO_POOL_MAX_ORDER already records this, so the coupling is not
lost with the macro.

cl_io.c:1596 (unit check robot): the flagged expression, npages -
head, no longer exists; the count is now built up in a local.

Response prepared with Claude Code.

Patch Set 4:

(6 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Mostly good. I walked the head/middle/tail decomposition, the partial-failure free path and the reworked copy loop (including short copies and the write-side cap) and did not find a correctness problem: entries always sum to the page span, cl_page_clip() only ever lands on order 0 entries, the copy loop always ends on the last entry, and every written entry is flushed exactly once. The inline comments are all minor - two kernel-version references that do not check out, a comment rationale the patch's own numbers contradict, and some cdp_npgs handling that this patch makes dead. None of them needs a re-spin on their own; fold them in whenever the patch is next refreshed. One coverage thought: sanity test_119h already compares unaligned against aligned DIO at sizes that produce multi-page entries, but the new short-buffer behaviour (request capped to half the order 0 pool, caller loops instead of getting -EINVAL) has no test - would a case that shrinks the pool via `pool_max_memory_mb` and drives a DIO larger than the cap be worth adding?

commit.subject: LU-19895 clio: use large folios for unaligned DIO
commit.message:
LU-19895 clio: use large folios for unaligned DIO

The unaligned DIO bounce buffer was filled from the order 0
pool, one page and one cl_page per PAGE_SIZE, so it never
benefited from the multi-order folio extents the aligned path
now builds.  It matters more than the aligned case in practice:
the client allocates this buffer itself, so no THP backed user
buffer is needed, and hybrid IO routes ordinary buffered writes
into exactly this path.

Fill the buffer from the compound page pools: the bulk from the
largest order which fits (within one brw_ext), the remainder
from order 0.  Per-chunk bookkeeping falls from one
cl_page/oap/brw_ext per PAGE_SIZE to one per folio extent -
16384 entries to ~320 for a 64MiB chunk.

The buffer is capped at half the order 0 pool and the caller
loops; previously a request above the pool limit failed with
-EINVAL.  A zero length request still fails with -EINVAL.
Encrypted files keep order 0 entries (cdp_no_coalesce).

The read side now selects copy_folio_to_iter() on a dedicated
LC_HAVE_COPY_FOLIO_TO_ITER probe rather than inferring it from
the older __filemap_get_folio(), which does not imply it: the
former arrived in v5.19, the latter in v5.16, so kernels in
between did not build.

Generated with Claude Code + Tools

Fixes: 59d84ec3ffb8 ("LU-19249 build: Compatibility updates for kernel v6.16")
Signed-off-by: Patrick Farrell <patrick@thelustrecollective.com>
